title: Surrounded Regions
description:
You are given an `m x n` matrix `board` containing the characters `'X'` and `'O'`. Capture all regions that are **4-directionally surrounded** by `'X'`.

A region is formed by connecting adjacent `'O'` cells horizontally or vertically (diagonals are not connected). A region is **surrounded** if none of its `'O'` cells lie on the border (first row, last row, first column, or last column) of the board.

To capture a surrounded region, flip every `'O'` cell in that region to `'X'` **in-place** in the given `board`. Regions connected to any border `'O'` must remain `'O'`.
hints: Instead of trying to determine which interior `'O'` regions are fully surrounded, think in reverse: which `'O'` cells can *never* be captured?
Any `'O'` on the border—and any `'O'` reachable from a border `'O'` via 4-directional `'O'` steps—cannot be surrounded.

Run BFS or DFS from every border `'O'`, temporarily marking all safe cells with a placeholder such as `'S'`. Then scan the board once more: flip remaining `'O'` cells to `'X'` and restore `'S'` cells back to `'O'`.

examples.explanation: The three interior 'O' cells form a region with no border contact and are flipped to 'X', while the bottom-border 'O' at (3, 1) cannot be captured.
A 1x1 board with 'X' has no 'O' regions to capture.
The single center 'O' at (1, 1) is completely surrounded on all four sides by 'X', so it is flipped to 'X'.
